* fix(stablecoins): rows name the issuer of record beside the brand, and filter by assetType (spec 1.9.121)

GET /api/stablecoins served one `company` field, a curated brand, and it
read as the issuer: AUDD said Novatti Group where its stellar.toml
ORG_NAME is AUDC PTY LTD, and the eight C1 rows said Currency One where
it is Kinesis Money Panama S.A. ?assetType= answered 400, so yield
products could not be left out.

- issuerOfRecord, issuerOfRecordSourceUrl, issuerOfRecordAsOf and
  issuerOfRecordNote: the ORG_NAME in the stellar.toml at the issuer
  account's home_domain (from Horizon), counted only when that toml lists
  the account. The 6-hourly refresh writes them: null until its first
  read, the last read kept whole on a later miss, never taken from
  company. The note quotes a currency desc that names another issuing
  party (MGUSD: issued by Bridge on behalf of MoneyGram).
- assetType filter: Yield Stablecoin, Treasury-Backed or none, a closed
  set answering 400 with the valid values. assetType null is documented
  as unclassified, no longer as a plain peg.
- The spec documents company as the brand, issuerDomain as the curated
  domain (12 of 41 differ from the account's home_domain), country as the
  peg's country, getRwaAssets issuerEntity as the rwa.xyz label, and
  declares paymentsCount24h.
- verifyClaim issued matches the issuer of record and the party the toml
  names as well as the brand; "is AUDD issued by AUDC PTY LTD" was

* fix(ai-chat): stop a cancelled queued chat request from running (#2818)

* fix(ai-chat): stop a cancelled queued chat request from running

A cancel sent while a request waited in the queue found no abort controller
and was dropped, so the request ran anyway once it reached the front. Create
the controller when the request is accepted, and skip onChatMessage if it
was cancelled before its turn started.

Fixes #2701

* fix(ai-chat): keep a cancelled queued request from replacing the stored request context

The abort check ran after _setRequestContext, so a request cancelled while
queued still overwrote the body and client tools that tool continuations
and continueLastTurn read. Check before writing them.

* fix(mcp): re-authorization and connection failures for the MCP client

Fixes #2658.

Re-authorization: a request that needs the user again (scope step-up, or
a 401 whose refresh fails) throws MCPAuthorizationRequiredError with a
link and moves the server to authenticating. OAuth flows take turns per
connection, re-authorization stops after three rounds for the same scopes
(MCP spec step-up limit), a declined step-up keeps the session on its
current grant, and a request made before the first authorization gets the
pending link.

Connection failures: each connect makes the server's quick attempts
(connect plus discovery), then records the failure. A failed server stays
failed across wakes until reconnectMcpServer(id); refused authorization
skips the attempts. addMcpServer() for a registered server reports its
state as is; a waiting server keeps its link until reconnected.

The manager is split into a facade and controllers (servers,
authorization, status), with per-server lanes for connection work.
Integration tests run an Agent against an OAuth MCP server served through
msw.

* fix(mcp): a late OAuth exchange leaves a re-added server's flow alone; stale-session recovery keeps its link; a declined step-up survives a wake

- Work for a server added again waits for the removed server's running
  work, so a late code exchange cannot delete the new flow's discovery
  state, and it clears only its own tokens.
- Recovering a forgotten session records what discovery found, including
  a link when only the catalog needs OAuth.
- A declined step-up on a server that still holds tokens reconnects on
  that grant when the session it ran on is gone.

* fix(mcp): remember that a pending link is a step-up, so a decline after a wake resumes only a step-up

The flag is stored with the link (pending_step_up), so a fresh sign-in
that the user declines is still recorded, whatever tokens are stored.
The resume starts from the callback handling itself, so standalone
callers of handleCallbackRequest() get it too.

* fix(mcp): send transport.headers from registerServer(), and name a rejected 401 for what it is

Fixes #2822. Fixes #2824.

The connection applies transport.headers when it builds an HTTP transport
(requestInit for every request, eventSourceInit.fetch for the SSE stream),
so registerServer() and restored connections send them, not only
addMcpServer(). A 401 from a server with no OAuth provider now says the
server rejected the request and to check the credentials.

coordinatorCorrectionReadback.body:
A source-date correction from the 2026-11-06 recheck:

- [SDF's CCTP announcement](https://stellar.org/blog/foundation-news/circle-cctp-is-live-on-stellar) now shows May 19, 2026. Its published timestamp is `2026-05-19T14:00:00.000Z`.
- [Circle's 2026 release notes](https://developers.circle.com/release-notes/cctp-2026) list Stellar mainnet support under `2026.05.18`.

These sources now support two distinct milestones. The issue's May 8 reference does not describe the current SDF page.
The wording that treats May 18 and May 19 as unsupported also needs that qualification.
This recheck does not establish what the page showed during the original July observation.

Lumenloop article `6461` currently agrees with the May 19 publication timestamp.
We have not reproduced an incorrect date in its content, or established that a previous content defect was fixed.
The request to preserve separately typed milestone provenance remains open; this comment corrects its supporting evidence only.
